title: No X25519 hybrid group exists for ML-KEM-1024 in oqs-provider 0.12.0
Hybrid ClientHello key_share is an order of magnitude larger than X25519
Hybrid handshake latency overhead over X25519 is measurable but small in absolute terms
Implicit rejection is silent: tampered ciphertexts return success with a pseudorandom secret
The decapsulation API takes no ciphertext length, so the FIPS 203 length check is the caller's job
Only X25519MLKEM768 is RFC 10024 Recommended; pre-standard draft groups are obsolete
ML-KEM-768 is the FIPS 203 recommended default; parameter-set choice is a security-category choice
Hybrid share ordering differs by group: ML-KEM secret first for X25519, ECDHE first for SecP groups
Server CPU per hybrid handshake is higher than classical, dominated by ML-KEM operations
Encapsulation randomness is recoverable by the decapsulator, so a weak random-bit generator compromises both algorithms
